Privacy Policy

Last updated: [[EFFECTIVE_DATE]]

  • We collect what the game needs to run: your sign-in, your game progress, and what you say to other players.
  • No ads, no third-party tracking, no analytics cookies. We keep our own record of how the game is played (how long, and which parts) to make it better. We don't sell or share your data for advertising.
  • Payments go through Stripe. We never see your card.
  • Settings, Download my data gives you a copy of everything we hold about you. Settings, Delete account erases it.

1. Who's responsible

[[OPERATOR]], [[ADDRESS]], is the controller of your personal data for Wayfolk. Contact us about privacy at [[CONTACT_EMAIL]].

2. What we collect, and why

What Why Legal basis (GDPR)
Account: your email and a hashed password (we never store the password itself), or your Google account ID and email if you sign in with Google. Guests get a random login and password kept in their browser. To sign you in, keep your account safe, and send password-reset and confirm emails. Contract
Game data: your display name, heroes, gold, items, journal, guild, friends, your profile (what you write about yourself, and whether it's private), blocks, market listings, buy orders and sales, trades with other players (who, and what each gave), mail (letters you send and receive: who, the note, and what's in them), event contributions, card-table stats, cosmetics, and when you last played. To run the game and show leaderboards. Contract
Messages: whispers to friends (the last 50 between each pair are kept). Public, guild and table chat is shown to other players and kept only in the server's memory for a short while - it isn't saved. To deliver messages. Contract
Reports and moderation: when someone reports a chat line, that line and the 10 lines before it, who reported whom, and any mute. To keep chat safe. Legitimate interests (player safety)
Subscription: your Stripe customer ID and your subscription's status and end date. Stripe holds your payment details and billing address; we don't. To give Supporter perks while you're subscribed. Contract; legal obligation (tax records)
Connection data: your IP address while you're connected. To limit sign-up spam and password guessing. It's held in memory only, not saved with your account. Legitimate interests (security)
How you play: when each visit starts and ends, how much of it you were playing and how much the game sat idle (the tab hidden, or nothing pressed for two minutes), how long you'd been away, your device type (desktop, tablet or phone), the website or link that brought you on your first visit, and how often each day you open each window and use each feature. Kept on our own server; nothing goes to an analytics company. To see which parts of the game work, where new players get stuck, and what to improve. Legitimate interests (improving the game)
Feedback: what you write in the Feedback window, what it's about, when, the game's version and your device type. To fix what's wrong and hear what you'd like. Staff read it. Legitimate interests (improving the game)
Server logs and error reports: your player ID and display name when you sign in or out, and errors. When the game hits an error, in your browser or on our server, a report goes to Sentry: what went wrong, your player ID and display name, your browser and device type, and the page address. To keep the game working and fix problems. Legitimate interests

We don't use your data for advertising or profiling, and we don't make automated decisions about you that have legal or similarly significant effects. The automatic chat mute (section 5 of the Terms) is temporary, and you can ask a moderator to review it.

3. What other players see

Other players can see your display name, Supporter badge and name colour, guild, what you say in public, guild and table chat, leaderboard rankings, your profile (what you write on it, the month you started, your heroes' names, looks and levels, and stats such as events joined and hands of cards played; if you make it private, only your friends see more than your name), your market listings and buy orders, what you offer in a trade with them, letters you send them, and whether you're online. Friends can also see what your heroes are doing. Your email is never shown to other players.

4. Storage in your browser

We don't use cookies. The game keeps a few things in your browser's local storage, all needed for it to work as you've asked, so there's no consent banner:

Name What it's for How long
wf_guestLogin, wf_guestPassword A guest account's sign-in Until you save the account, or clear your browser
wf_remember "Remember me": signs this browser straight in Until you sign out, or it expires
wf_session, wf_resume Signs you back in if the connection drops (this tab only) Until you close the tab
wf_email The last email typed on the sign-in screen, filled in for you Until you clear your browser
wf_sound, wf_effects, wf_chatSwearing Your sound, effects and chat-filter settings Until you clear your browser

If you choose Sign in with Google, Google's sign-in button is loaded from Google and Google may set its own cookies (see Google's privacy policy). Stripe's checkout page is on Stripe's own site, under Stripe's privacy policy.

5. Who we share it with

We only share data with the services that help us run the game, under contracts that protect it:

  • Stripe - payments (if you subscribe).
  • Google - sign-in (if you use Sign in with Google).
  • Sentry (Functional Software, Inc.) - error reports, so we can fix what broke.
  • [[EMAIL_PROVIDER]] - sending account emails.
  • [[HOSTING_PROVIDER]] - the servers the game runs on.

We may also share data if the law requires it, to protect players from harm (for example, reporting child-safety concerns), or if the game is sold to someone who'll keep running it under this policy. We don't sell your personal information, and we don't "share" it for cross-context advertising as California law defines it.

Some of these services may process data outside your country, including in the United States. Where that happens we rely on safeguards such as the EU Standard Contractual Clauses or the EU-US Data Privacy Framework.

6. How long we keep it

  • Your account and game data: until you delete your account. A guest account (one not saved with an email or Google) is deleted, with everything in it, once nobody has signed in to it for 180 days: it only works from the browser that made it, so after that long it has almost always been lost.
  • Sign-in tokens and email links: "remember me" lasts 30 days from when it was last used; reset links work for an hour and confirm links for 7 days. All are deleted with your account.
  • How you play: your visits until you delete your account; which windows and features you used each day, for 90 days. Feedback you send: until you delete your account.
  • Error reports: Sentry deletes them after 90 days at most.
  • Chat reports: until moderators have dealt with them, and at most until your account (or the reported account) is deleted.
  • Backups: deleted data can stay in database backups for up to [[BACKUP_DAYS]] days before they're overwritten.
  • Payment records: Stripe keeps records of payments as the law requires, even after you delete your account.

7. Your rights

Wherever you live, you can:

  • Get a copy of your data - Settings, then Download my data. You get a JSON file with your account, heroes, items, friends, whispers, guild, market history and more.
  • Delete your account - Settings, then Delete account. This erases your data straight away (apart from what's described in section 6) and cancels any subscription.
  • Correct your data - change your display name in Settings; for anything else, email us.
  • Object or restrict - email us if you object to how we use your data.

If you're in the EU, UK or a similar place, these are your rights under the GDPR, and you can also complain to your local data protection authority. If you're in California, you have the rights to know, delete, correct and opt out under the CCPA/CPRA; we won't treat you differently for using them. Since we don't sell or share personal information, there's nothing to opt out of.

If you can't use the buttons in Settings (say you've lost access to your account), email us from the account's address and we'll help. We reply within 30 days.

8. Children

The game isn't meant for children under 13, and we don't knowingly collect their data. If you think a child under 13 has an account, email us and we'll delete it.

9. Security

Passwords are hashed, sign-in tokens are stored hashed, and the game is served over an encrypted connection. No system is perfect; if something goes wrong that affects your data, we'll tell you and the authorities as the law requires.

10. Changes

If we change this policy in a way that matters, we'll tell you in the game before the change takes effect.

Questions? Email [[CONTACT_EMAIL]].
